funding_agencies.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

series_statement.series_info: This is the fifth GSHS conducted by Philippines.

study_info.abstract: The GSHS is a school-based survey which uses a self-administered questionnaire to obtain data on young people's health behaviour and protective factors related to the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among children and adults worldwide.
study_info.geog_coverage: National plus Luzon, Mindanao and Visayas.
study_info.notes:
The following core modules were included in the survey:
alcohol use
dietary behaviours
drug use
hygiene
mental health
physical activity
protective factors
violence and unintentional injury

data_collection.sampling_procedure: A two-stage cluster sample design was used to produce data representative of all students in grades 7-Fourth Year in the Philippines. At the first stage, schools were selected with probability proportional to enrollment size. At the second stage, classes were randomly selected and all students in selected classes were eligible to participate.

data_collection.weight:
The weighting formula used is:
W=W1 * W2 * f1 * f2 * f3.
The list below shows what each variable in the formula represents.
W1 - The inverse of the probability of selecting each school
W2 - The inverse of the probability of selecting each classroom
f1 - A school-level non response adjustment factor
f2 - A student-level non response adjustment factor calculated by classroom
f3 - A post stratification adjustment factor calculated by sex within grade
data_collection.cleaning_operations: All data processing (scanning, cleaning, editing, and weighting) was conducted at WHO and the US Centers for Disease Control.

analysis_info.response_rate: The school response rate was 100%, the student response rate was 85%, and the overall response rate was 85%.

dataset_use.cit_req:
Publications based on GSHS data should use the following acknowledgement:
"This paper uses data from the Global School-Based Student Health Survey (GSHS). GSHS is supported by the World Health Organization and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention."
